blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Every tax has its own deadline. VAT returns are usually due every quarter. Corporate tax is due once a year, often several months after the financial year ends. Payroll taxes run every month, with the salaries. Each tax has its own form, its own date, and its own penalty if it slips.

A good company puts them all on one calendar at the start of the year. It gives each deadline an owner. Every Monday, the team looks at next month's deadlines.

It is not exciting, but nothing slips. The calendar turns tax from a series of surprises into a quiet routine — which is exactly what tax should be.

items.q: How often are VAT returns usually due?
items.why: "VAT returns are usually due every quarter."

items.q: When does the team look at next month's deadlines?
options: At the end of the year
items.why: "Every Monday, the team looks at next month's deadlines."

items.q: What happens if a company misses a deadline?
items.why: "its own penalty if it slips" — perder o prazo gera multa.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Reviewing deadlines weekly is a good habit.
One calendar helps a company stay organised.
It is safe to remember each deadline in your head.
Each deadline should have an owner.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende um calendário único e revisão semanal, não a memória de cada um.

items.q: "A quiet routine — which is exactly what tax should be" suggests that…
options: tax should be calm and predictable
tax is the most exciting part of work
tax does not need any planning
tax should be full of surprises
items.why: Inferência: "quiet routine" indica que o imposto deveria ser calmo e previsível, sem sustos.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily montando o calendário fiscal da empresa. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, I am building our tax calendar on one page. One A4 page for the whole year. Every deadline, every owner, every form — all in one place.

Let me go through it. Payroll taxes are due every month, so I put them on the fifteenth of each month. VAT returns are due every quarter, so I mark April, July, October, and January. Corporate tax is due once a year, in March, a few months after our financial year ends.

Now, the owners. I do not want one person to carry everything. So payroll goes to Tom, VAT goes to me, and corporate tax goes to Sarah. Each name sits next to each date, so we always know who is responsible.

And here is the important part. Every Monday, we look at next month's deadlines together. Just five minutes. If we do that, nothing slips, and we never pay a penalty. It is not exciting work, but a calm routine is exactly what I want with tax. No surprises.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: On how many pages is Emily building the calendar?
items.why: "One A4 page for the whole year."

items.q: When is corporate tax due?
items.why: "Corporate tax is due once a year, in March."

items.q: Who is the owner of the VAT returns?
items.why: "VAT goes to me" — Emily fala em primeira pessoa.

items.q: Why does Emily give each tax a different owner?
options: So one person does not carry everything
Because she has too many pages
items.why: Inferência: "I do not want one person to carry everything" — ela divide a responsabilidade.

items.q: What does Emily believe the Monday review will prevent?
items.why: Inferência: "nothing slips, and we never pay a penalty" — a revisão evita prazos perdidos e multas.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We missed the deadline, so we paid a small fine." A deadline is…
options: the last date to do something
items.why: Deadline = prazo, a última data para fazer algo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The company pays a ___ every time it sends a form late."
items.why: Penalty = multa, o que se paga por atraso.

items.q: "Our financial year ends in December." The financial year is…
options: the twelve months a company uses for its accounts
the busiest month of the year
items.why: Financial year = ano fiscal, os doze meses usados nas contas da empresa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The payroll tax is paid every month, with the ___."
items.why: Payroll = folha de pagamento; o imposto sai junto com os salários.

items.q: "Every deadline has an owner." Here, an owner is…
options: the person who owns the company
items.why: Owner = responsável, quem cuida daquele prazo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre impostos e prazos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the tax calendar." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new calendar next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em uso, implementar.

items.q: "Please keep track of every deadline." To keep track of means to…
items.why: Keep track of = acompanhar, não perder de vista.

items.q: "The VAT deadline is coming up soon." Coming up means it is…
items.why: Coming up = está chegando, vai acontecer em breve.

items.q: "Let's follow through and file the form on time." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
